title: HDX-MS Combining Molecular Dynamics Simulation Reveals Structural Basis of Transcriptional Coactivator PC4 Binding to a Platinum Crosslinked Double-Stranded DNA
authors: Yuanyuan Wang; Zhifeng Du; Lifang Chen; Yao Zhao; Wei Zheng; Juan Qiao; Kui Wu; Hui Zhang; Qun Luo; Li Qi; Xin Zhang; Fuyi Wang
one_liner_zh: 该文结合HDX-MS与分子动力学模拟，解析转录共激活因子PC4与铂交联双链DNA的结合界面与动态互作机制，属广义蛋白-DNA互作且方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Human nuclear protein positive cofactor PC4 is a DNA-binding protein, and plays an important role in the early response to DNA damage by recognizing single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide domain and facilitating the subsequent steps of DNA repair. Our group previously discovered that PC4 selectively binds to a double-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (dsODN) damaged by a trans-platinum anticancer complex, trans-[PtCl2(NH3)(thiazole)] (trans-PtTz). However, the molecular basis of this unique recognition and interaction remained unclear. In this work, amide hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) was applied to dissect the interaction interface between PC4 and a 15-mer double-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide crosslinked by trans-PtTz (trans-PtTz-dsODN). Global deuterium uptake suggested a 1:1 binding stoichiometry of PC4 to trans-PtTz-dsODN. Local deuterium uptake revealed that the flexible N-terminal loop and the β3 – β5-sheet played key roles in the recognition and interaction between PC4 and trans-PtTz-dsODN. In order to locate the key amino acid residues, molecular dynamics simulation was employed, demonstrating that PC4 binds to the trans-PtTz-dsODN at the minor groove via strong H-bonds with the nucleobases of the complementary strand. The minor groove width was broadened to adapt for the binding of PC4. Arg86 residue in PC4 was shown to dominate the recognition and interaction, which was verified by electrophoretic mobility shift assays. This work profiles the detailed interaction mechanism of PC4 with trans-PtTz damaged dsODN, and the combination use of HDX-MS and molecular dynamics simulation provides a new paradigm for the future research of the cellular response to the platinum induced DNA damage.
abstract_zh: 人核蛋白正协同因子PC4是一种DNA结合蛋白，通过识别单链寡脱氧核苷酸结构域并促进DNA修复的后续步骤，在DNA损伤的早期反应中发挥重要作用。我们课题组先前发现，PC4选择性地结合由反式铂抗癌复合物trans-[PtCl2(NH3)(噻唑)] (trans-PtTz)损伤的双链寡脱氧核苷酸 (dsODN)。然而，这种独特识别和相互作用的分子基础仍不清楚。在本工作中，应用酰胺氢/氘交换质谱 (HDX-MS) 解析PC4与由trans-PtTz交联的15-mer双链寡脱氧核苷酸 (trans-PtTz-dsODN) 之间的相互作用界面。整体氘摄取表明PC4与trans-PtTz-dsODN的结合化学计量比为1:1。局部氘摄取揭示，柔性N端环和β3–β5折叠片在PC4与trans-PtTz-dsODN的识别和相互作用中发挥关键作用。为定位关键氨基酸残基，采用分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，表明PC4通过互补链核碱基的强氢键结合于trans-PtTz-dsODN的小沟。小沟宽度被拓宽以适应PC4的结合。PC4中的Arg86残基被证明主导识别和相互作用，并通过电泳迁移率变动分析得到验证。本工作描绘了PC4与trans-PtTz损伤dsODN相互作用的详细机制，且HDX-MS与分子动力学模拟的联合使用为未来铂诱导DNA损伤细胞响应的研究提供了新范式。
